# Siren core — timeline effect vocabulary (exit, highlight, slide, prev)

## Problem

The first vertical slice proved the parse-to-animated-render pipeline end to end, but the
`timeline:` syntax only supports one action (`enter <id> fade`) — none of the effects the product
was originally scoped for exist yet: elements can't disappear (`exit`), can't be highlighted after
appearing (`highlight`/`unhighlight`), and `enter` only has one visual style (`fade`, no
directional slide). There's also no way to step backward through a timeline once played forward.
Going deeper on the existing flowchart + timeline foundation (rather than adding new diagram types
or markdown integration) means completing this vocabulary before anything else is worth building.

## Outcome

An author can write a `timeline:` block using four verbs — `enter`, `exit`, `highlight`,
`unhighlight` — where `enter`/`exit` accept an effect of `fade` or a directional
`slide-{left,right,top,bottom}`, and `highlight` accepts `outline` or `glow`. `unhighlight` takes
no effect, just a target id. `render()`'s returned controller gains `prev()` alongside the
existing `next()`/`reset()`, jumping instantly (no animation) to the state the diagram would be in
after that many `next()` calls from the start. All of this is verified through the same layered
seams as the first slice — unit tests for parser/graph-model, jsdom component tests for
renderer/animation, an integration test through `render()`, and a browser demo for visual
confirmation.

## Scope

- Parser: recognize `exit`, `highlight`, `unhighlight` as timeline verbs alongside the existing
  `enter`; recognize `slide-left`/`slide-right`/`slide-top`/`slide-bottom` as effect names for
  `enter`/`exit` in addition to `fade`; recognize `outline`/`glow` as effect names for `highlight`;
  `unhighlight <id>` parses with no effect token.
- Graph model: resolve all four action kinds against declared node/edge ids (existing
  unknown-id-diagnostic behavior generalizes); validate that a `highlight`/`exit`/`unhighlight`
  action's step is not before the step its target becomes visible (own `enter` step, or step 0 if
  never entered) — a violation is an error diagnostic, the action is dropped, the rest of the
  graph still builds; a target given more than one `enter` (or more than one `exit`) keeps the
  first occurrence and emits a warning diagnostic, matching the existing duplicate-node-id
  convention.
- Renderer: fix the initial-`siren-pending` computation to only elements with an `enter` action —
  today it (incorrectly, for this next slice) marks anything referenced anywhere in the timeline,
  which would wrongly hide an element whose only timeline action is `exit` or `highlight`.
- Animation runtime: `next()` applies whichever action(s) are assigned to the newly-current step —
  `enter` swaps `siren-pending` for `siren-enter-{effect}`; `exit` adds `siren-exit-{effect}`
  (element stays in the DOM, ends hidden/off-screen, held there by the same transition mechanism
  as today's fade); `highlight` adds `siren-highlight-{effect}`, replacing any highlight effect
  already active on that element; `unhighlight` removes whichever `siren-highlight-*` class is
  present. `prev()` moves `currentStep` back by one and sets DOM state to match what it would be
  had only `next()` been called `currentStep` times from the start — instantly, no transition.
  `reset()` is unchanged (already instant).
- Public API: `AnimationController.prev(): void` is exposed through `render()`'s returned
  controller; new graph-model diagnostics propagate through the same `diagnostics` array as today.
- Demo: `examples/step-reveal.srn` and `demos/step-reveal.html`/`.css` updated to exercise
  `exit`, `highlight`/`unhighlight`, at least one `slide-*` effect, and a new "Prev" button.

## Non-goals

- Any effect beyond the ones listed (no bounce, no scale, no rotate, no custom easing/duration
  authored in the syntax) — deferred.
- Reverse-animated `prev()` (playing exit-style transitions backward) — explicitly rejected this
  round in favor of an instant snap; may be revisited later, but as its own decision.
- An element having more than one `enter` or more than one `exit` action treated as anything other
  than "first wins, warn" — no support for re-entering after exiting, no toggling in and out
  repeatedly within one timeline.
- `goTo(step)` / arbitrary seeking beyond `next()`/`prev()`/`reset()`.
- Autoplay/timers — still caller-driven only.
- Any diagram type other than flowchart; markdown embedding; VS Code extension; website;
  playground — unchanged from the first slice's non-goals.

## Domain decisions

- **Timeline action kinds**: four verbs — `enter`, `exit`, `highlight`, `unhighlight`. `enter` and
  `exit` take an effect name from `{fade, slide-left, slide-right, slide-top, slide-bottom}`.
  `highlight` takes an effect name from `{outline, glow}`. `unhighlight` takes no effect — just a
  target id.
- **Slide direction semantics**: for `enter`, `slide-left` means the element arrives *from* the
  left (enters moving rightward into place). For `exit`, `slide-left` means the element departs
  *toward* the left (leaves moving leftward, off its original position) — the same direction name
  means opposite motion depending on the verb, matching how an author would read it aloud ("slide
  [in from the] left" vs "slide [out to the] left").
- **Visibility precondition**: an element becomes "visible" either from the start (step 0, never
  mentioned with `enter`) or at its own `enter` step. A `highlight`, `exit`, or `unhighlight`
  action naming that element at a step *before* it becomes visible is invalid — error diagnostic,
  action dropped, rest of the graph still builds. A step equal to the element's own `enter` step is
  valid (an element can enter and be highlighted in the same step).
- **Highlight is cumulative, not exclusive**: multiple elements can be highlighted simultaneously.
  A second `highlight` action on an already-highlighted element replaces its effect (e.g.
  `outline` → `glow`) without needing an `unhighlight` in between. Only `unhighlight` (or nothing,
  if never highlighted) means "not highlighted."
- **`exit` keeps the element in the DOM**: matches the existing `siren-pending` philosophy — the
  element becomes invisible (opacity 0 / translated off, per effect) but is never removed, so
  `prev()` can restore it without a re-render.
- **`prev()` is instant, not a reverse animation**: `prev()` sets `currentStep` back by one and
  applies the DOM state that corresponds to that step's cumulative history, with no CSS
  transition — the same "just move the class, let the shipped stylesheet's `transition` decide
  timing" contract as `next()`, except `prev()`'s target classes carry no transition, only the
  `next()`-driven ones do (an implementation detail: the *shipped stylesheet* is responsible for
  not giving `prev()`'s snap classes a `transition` declaration, not the animation runtime code —
  see the Renderer/Animation module notes for how this is expected to be expressed as CSS, not JS
  timing logic).
- **Duplicate `enter`/`exit` per element**: first occurrence wins, warning diagnostic — matches the
  existing duplicate-node-id convention rather than introducing a new hard-error category.
- **SVG/CSS class conventions (extending the first slice's)**:
  - `siren-pending` — unchanged: present iff the element has an `enter` action, before it fires.
  - `siren-enter-{effect}` — added (replacing `siren-pending`) when an `enter` action fires.
  - `siren-exit-{effect}` — added when an `exit` action fires. The element had no `siren-pending`
    class before this (it must already be visible per the precondition above).
  - `siren-highlight-{effect}` — added when a `highlight` action fires; removed when `unhighlight`
    fires, or replaced (old removed, new added) when a later `highlight` action targets the same
    element.

## Design contract

### `packages/core/src/contracts.ts` (extend, don't redefine unrelated types)

- Changes: `TimelineAction`/`ResolvedTimeline`-shaped types generalize from "enter only" to
  `{ kind: 'enter' | 'exit' | 'highlight' | 'unhighlight'; step: number; targetId: string; effect?: EnterExitEffect | HighlightEffect }`
  (effect present for `enter`/`exit`/`highlight`, absent for `unhighlight`). New effect union
  types: `EnterExitEffect = 'fade' | 'slide-left' | 'slide-right' | 'slide-top' | 'slide-bottom'`,
  `HighlightEffect = 'outline' | 'glow'`. `AnimationController` gains `prev(): void`.
- Seam: same as before — this file is the frozen contract every module below builds against
  without waiting on each other's implementations.

### Parser (`packages/core/src/parser/`)

- Responsibilities: extend the existing `timeline:` line grammar to the four verbs and their
  effect vocabularies above; report a diagnostic (not a throw) for an unrecognized verb or effect
  name, same as today's "unsupported effect" handling.
- Non-responsibilities: still does not check that targets exist or are visible in time — that
  stays graph-model's job.
- Interface: `parseSiren` signature unchanged; `SirenDocument`'s timeline shape carries the
  generalized action type above.
- Seam: `parseSiren(source)` — unit level, pure function, unchanged from the first slice.

### Graph model (`packages/core/src/graph-model/`)

- Responsibilities: resolve all four action kinds against declared ids; compute each element's
  "becomes visible at step" (0, or its own `enter` step) and validate every `highlight`/`exit`/
  `unhighlight` action's step against it; apply first-wins/warn for duplicate `enter`/`exit`.
- Interface: `buildGraphModel` signature unchanged; `GraphModel.timeline` carries the generalized
  `ResolvedTimeline`.
- Seam: `buildGraphModel(document)` — unit level, pure function, hand-built `SirenDocument`
  fixtures, unchanged from the first slice.

### Renderer (`packages/core/src/renderer/`)

- Responsibilities: fix `pendingElementIds` (or equivalent) to mark `siren-pending` only for
  elements with an `enter` action in the resolved timeline — not "any timeline entry" as today.
  Everything else about `renderToSVG` (SVG structure, sizing, text centering) is unchanged.
- Interface: `renderToSVG(graph: PositionedGraph): SVGSVGElement` — unchanged signature.
- Seam: unchanged — jsdom component tests, hand-built `PositionedGraph` fixtures.

### Animation runtime (`packages/core/src/animation/`)

- Responsibilities: `next()` applies every action assigned to the newly-current step, per action
  kind, using the class rules in Domain decisions; `prev()` recomputes and applies the DOM class
  state for `currentStep - 1`'s cumulative history, instantly; `reset()` unchanged. The exact
  internal method (e.g., replaying history vs. diffing) is an implementation choice, not part of
  this contract — only the observable end state is.
- Interface: `createAnimationController(svg, timeline): AnimationController` where
  `AnimationController = { totalSteps; currentStep; next(): void; prev(): void; reset(): void }`.
- Seam: unchanged — jsdom component tests, hand-built SVG + `ResolvedTimeline` fixtures.

### Public API (`packages/core/src/index.ts`)

- Responsibilities: no pipeline changes — `render()` already composes the modules above; this
  ticket only needs to confirm `prev()` reaches the caller through the returned controller and
  that new graph-model diagnostics surface in `result.diagnostics`.
- Interface: `render(source, container, options?)` — unchanged signature.
- Seam: unchanged — jsdom integration test.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `enter`/`exit` parse and resolve `fade` and all four `slide-*` names; `highlight` parses and
      resolves `outline`/`glow`; `unhighlight <id>` parses with no effect token.
- [ ] An `exit` action's target starts visible (no `siren-pending`), and firing it (via `next()`)
      adds `siren-exit-{effect}` while the element remains present in the DOM.
- [ ] An element with only `exit`/`highlight` actions (no `enter`) never gets `siren-pending` at
      any point — confirms the renderer fix.
- [ ] Two `highlight` actions on the same element with different effects at different steps result
      in only the second effect's class being present after both have fired (no stacking).
- [ ] `unhighlight` removes the currently-active `siren-highlight-*` class.
- [ ] A `highlight`/`exit`/`unhighlight` action whose step is before its target becomes visible
      produces an error diagnostic; the action is dropped; `render()` does not throw and the rest
      of the diagram still renders.
- [ ] After N `next()` calls, one `prev()` call produces DOM state indistinguishable (by class
      list, per element) from the state after N-1 `next()` calls, and does so without adding any
      of the `siren-enter-*`/`siren-exit-*` transition-triggering classes that weren't already the
      correct ones for step N-1.
- [ ] `demos/step-reveal.html` has a working "Prev" button, and its example document exercises
      `exit`, `highlight`+`unhighlight`, and at least one `slide-*` effect.

## Test strategy

- Parser/graph-model: unit, pure functions, same pattern as the first slice.
- Renderer/animation: jsdom component tests, hand-built fixtures.
- `render()`: jsdom integration test.
- Demo: manual/visual verification in a real browser, same as the first slice.

## Verification

- Focused: `pnpm --filter @siren/core test -- <file>`
- Suite: `pnpm --filter @siren/core test`
- Static: `pnpm --filter @siren/core exec tsc --noEmit`

## Baseline

Measured 2026-09-03, current `main` (`37b24dc` and after). 37 passing tests, 0 type errors. Do not
repair anything outside a ticket's own scope.

## Risks and deferred questions

- `prev()`'s "no transition" contract depends on the shipped demo stylesheet not attaching a
  `transition` to whatever class `prev()` applies — if a future slice reworks the CSS approach,
  this needs re-checking; not a risk to the animation runtime's own code, but to how the demo's
  CSS is authored.
- The "first `enter`/`exit` wins" rule (rather than a hard error) is a judgment call carried over
  from the first slice's duplicate-node-id precedent; revisit if authors report it as confusing in
  practice rather than helpful.
- Effect vocabulary (5 enter/exit effects, 2 highlight effects) is still hand-picked, not derived
  from any existing spec — same provisional status as the first slice's `timeline:` syntax itself
  (see ADR-0002).
